corpusSummary: Across 2026, this corpus documents how large language models and generative AI reshape social science inquiry and lived experience. Studies probe cognition, bias, and embodiment; position AI as a research instrument across disciplines; scrutinize AI’s roles in health, education, governance, and policy; and examine cultural, ethical, and existential dimensions of AI-mediated interaction. The overarching message stresses careful, context-aware use, validation, and attention to equity and safety.

themes.name: Trust, embodiment, and AI governance
themes.description: Research examines user trust, anthropomorphism, perceived humanness vs empathy, device embodiment, privacy, and equity considerations shaping AI adoption and governance.

themes.name: AI as a methodological tool for social science
themes.description: A growth of work positions LLMs as research tools for coding, data extraction, simulation, and policy prototyping, while stressing validation, transparency, and ethical standards.

themes.name: AI in education and health: benefits, risks, and literacy
themes.description: Evidence spans AI tutoring, learning outcomes, health information, misinformation, and the need for AI literacy and ethical guidelines in educational and clinical contexts.

themes.name: Cultural, spatial, and ethical dimensions of AI
themes.description: Literature explores AI’s impact on religion, heritage, sense of place, aesthetics, and digital mediation, highlighting limits of embodiment and cultural adaptation.
